lines.text: There's a weight you've been dragging so long, you've started calling it normal.
Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee.
You've carried it through every room where no one asked, and never once set it down.
So you knelt where nobody was watching, and finally let it show.
He is before all things, and by him all things consist.
The same hands holding galaxies together were never too occupied to hold what's breaking you.
So let the weight crack open at His feet, not yours.
What you couldn't carry another day, He was already carrying for you.

bold: The same hands holding galaxies together were never too occupied to hold what's breaking you.
title: Word and Faith Network
subtitle: What Holds You
story: A lone traveler drags a boulder across a dusk canyon, kneels exhausted beneath a vast starlit sky, and watches the stone crack open into gold light as dawn breaks and the weight finally lifts - a short visual parable of Psalm 55:22 and Colossians 1:17, on handing the thing you've been secretly dragging to the One who already holds everything together.
